brief: A workbench organizer: two storeys, bins on top, a drawer below, all edges capped.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.evidence: Bases on level 0 (piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;half-w, piece:1,-1,0;half-w, piece:1,-2,0;half-n) and level 1 (piece:0,0,1;full, piece:1,0,1;half-w, piece:1,-1,1;half-w) with snaps linking levels; check_build confirms two-level build.
Three bins on level 1: bin:0,0,1~hex-bin-full (full cell) and bin:1,0,1~hex-bin-half-w-half, bin:1,-1,1~hex-bin-half-w-half; all seated in top storey.
drawer:0#1,-2#cut installed on cut face of piece:1,-2,0;half-n at level 0.
15 solid caps placed via capOpenFaces (cap:0,0,0;*;150/210/270/90 etc.), joints locked with jointBolt:1#0,0#0/1; check_build shows no OPEN_CAP_FACE issues and meshClash clear.

finish.summary: Workbench organizer built as two-storey assembly: three bins on level 1 top, one drawer on level 0 lower, all perimeter edges capped and joints locked. check_build passes clear.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
